Package tests

Class LoginAttemptLimiterTestingAutomation

java.lang.Object
tests.LoginAttemptLimiterTestingAutomation
public class LoginAttemptLimiterTestingAutomation extends Object

Title: LoginAttemptLimiterTestingAutomation Class

Description: Automated tests for the failed-attempt limit of TP3 Aspect 5 (Staff log in securely and play the right role). They implement tests T-20 to T-26 of requirement TR-5 in TP3 Testing Details and Rationale.pdf, plus boundary and robustness tests written with them before the code existed, as test-driven development requires. The tests follow the team's style: a main method, one line of ***Success*** or ***Failure*** per check, and a count at the end.

The limit N and delay D are named constants so the tests do not change when Aspect 2 (Ronald) settles the real values.

    • testBelowLimit

      static void testBelowLimit()

      Method: void testBelowLimit()

      Description: T-20. N-1 failures, one below the limit, must not cause a delay, and the correct password then logs in and clears the count.

    • testAtLimit

      static void testAtLimit()

      Method: void testAtLimit()

      Description: T-21. N failures, exactly at the limit, must delay the username straight away and for the whole of D, so even the correct password is not checked.

    • testDelayEnds

      static void testDelayEnds()

      Method: void testDelayEnds()

      Description: T-22. The delay ends exactly at D, after which the username is allowed again with a fresh set of N attempts.

    • testSuccessResetsCount

      static void testSuccessResetsCount()

      Method: void testSuccessResetsCount()

      Description: T-23. Only consecutive failures count: N-1 failures, a success, and N-1 more failures must not cause a delay even though there were 2N-2 failures in total.

    • testOtherUsernamesUnaffected

      static void testOtherUsernamesUnaffected()

      Method: void testOtherUsernamesUnaffected()

      Description: T-24. The delay belongs to one username, so another staff member can still log in while the first is delayed.

    • testUnknownUsername

      static void testUnknownUsername()

      Method: void testUnknownUsername()

      Description: T-25. A username with no account is limited exactly like a real one, so the delay message cannot be used to find out which usernames exist.

    • testOnlyAdminNeverLockedOut

      static void testOnlyAdminNeverLockedOut()

      Method: void testOnlyAdminNeverLockedOut()

      Description: T-26. Even if someone keeps trying the only admin's username during the delay, the delay must not grow, so the admin can always log in once D has passed.

    • testRemainingDelay

      static void testRemainingDelay()

      Method: void testRemainingDelay()

      Description: Beyond the Task 4.2 list. The login page needs to tell the user how long to wait, so remainingDelay must count down and be zero when there is no delay.

    • testLimitOfOne

      static void testLimitOfOne()

      Method: void testLimitOfOne()

      Description: Beyond the Task 4.2 list. The smallest allowed limit is 1, so a single failure must start the delay. This is the lower boundary of N.

    • testNullUsername

      static void testNullUsername()

      Method: void testNullUsername()

      Description: Beyond the Task 4.2 list (CWE-476). The login page can pass an empty or missing username, and the limiter must treat null like the empty string, never throw.

    • testInvalidSettings

      static void testInvalidSettings()

      Method: void testInvalidSettings()

      Description: Beyond the Task 4.2 list. Settings that would switch the limit off or break it are refused when the limiter is created, rather than failing later at login.

    • testDefaultSettings

      static void testDefaultSettings()

      Method: void testDefaultSettings()

      Description: Beyond the Task 4.2 list. The no-argument constructor must use the named default settings so the login page can use it before Aspect 2 settles the values.
